description: Manage CI/CD pipelines from multiple providers (self hosted, desktop app and ios app )

summary.one_liner: Pipedash is a dashboard that shows pipelines and runs from many CI/CD providers in one table, available as a desktop app, a self-hosted Docker web server, or an iOS app.
summary.what_it_does: It polls each configured CI/CD provider using a token or kubeconfig and caches the results. Pipelines are grouped by repository and workflow, can be pinned or hidden, and can be organized into nested custom views with rule-based membership. From the table you can open run history, read and download job logs, trigger workflows with inputs, rerun runs, and cancel one or several runs. On GitHub it can also approve deployment reviews and rerun only failed jobs. ArgoCD sync details, per-resource results, events and pod container logs are viewable, and notifications fire on pipeline failure, unusually long runs or provider outages. Provider tokens are stored in the system keyring or an AES-256-GCM encrypted database.
use_cases: monitor CI/CD pipelines across multiple providers
find which build failed without switching dashboards
trigger or rerun a GitHub Actions or GitLab CI workflow
read and download job logs from CI runs
watch ArgoCD sync status and pod logs
get alerts when pipelines fail or run slowly
how_to_run: Download the desktop app from the project's releases page
Run the Docker image for the self-hosted web server
Follow the quick start guide to add your first provider
notable: Single shared Rust core powering desktop, self-hosted web and iOS apps
Plugin crate per provider, covering 11 CI/CD systems including Tekton, ArgoCD, FluxCD and Komodo
Nested custom views with rule-based membership (provider, repo pattern, name, status)
ArgoCD SSO sign-in via bundled Dex or external OIDC with automatic session renewal
Tokens encrypted with AES-256-GCM or kept in the system keyring; no telemetry
caveats: ArgoCD pod logs require the logs, get permission in ArgoCD RBAC
In the self-hosted web app, ArgoCD SSO requires pasting the post-sign-in page address unless Pipedash runs on the same machine as the browser
Some features such as approving deployments and rerunning failed jobs are described only for GitHub
keywords: see all builds in one place
